terra.problem: Saying he is in a hurry to get to her assigns an urgency and purpose the text does not state.
The passage describes the season of singing, but does not say mourning has no place in it.
The speaker asks to see her face, but the text does not say she is hiding or that he wants her to stop hiding.
The text says the vineyards are in bloom, not that they are undamaged. It does not say the foxes must be caught before damage starts.
The vineyards being in bloom does not establish that none have been ruined.
She does not find him, but the text does not establish that he was not there.
She does not find him, but the text does not establish that he is not there.
Saying she does not lie there hoping adds a detail about her thoughts that the text does not give.
The passage does not say the watchmen are paid or establish how well they know the city.
The earlier verse says her beloved pastures his flock; it does not say shepherds appeared.
The text does not say the watchmen are the people most likely to know what is out in the city.
The explanation is flat and repeats the same distinction without adding much to it.
Saying the watchmen barely had time to answer implies an answer or its timing, neither of which the text gives.
The text says she brings him to her mother's house, not that her family is there with them.
The passage does not say her mother's house is the home where she came from.
